questions.q: What makes up your Career Savings Account, according to Acuff's formula?
a: Relationships, skills, and character multiplied by hustle
Salary, title, and years of experience
Education, connections, and luck
Savings, investments, and side income
questions.why: Lesson 1 presents the account as relationships plus skills plus character, all multiplied by hustle.

questions.q: What does the summary say usually causes a career ceiling?
a: A gap in the skills you need to move up
A manager who dislikes you
Too few networking events
A company that is shrinking
questions.why: Lesson 2 says that when everything looks fine but nothing moves, you need an honest look at your skill gaps.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest you break through a career ceiling?
a: Add skills that complement your existing ones
Work longer hours than your colleagues
Apply for jobs at other companies
Ask for a raise and a new title
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends finding the skills that round out your strengths so you become ready for the next level.

questions.q: Which three character traits does Acuff say matter most?
a: Generosity, empathy, and presence
Ambition, patience, and resilience
Honesty, humour, and humility
Confidence, focus, and optimism
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists generosity, empathy, and presence as the traits he saw matter most over sixteen years.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest you can practise empathy?
a: Ask how you would feel in the other person's place
Listen without ever interrupting them
Share stories from your own life
Avoid judging anyone's choices out loud
questions.why: Lesson 3 says mentally stepping into another person's shoes helps you understand rather than judge them.
